# Instant order — Style Prompt

> The current launch-film grammar of software products, borrowed for anything that turns a request into a result: a request is typed into a clean rounded bar, a virtual camera dives at the button, and a hard cut lands on the finished thing. Proof follows as a burst of very short cuts, then the film exhales into a calm, almost empty end card. Everything is redrawn UI on a flat ground that alternates light and dark; the camera does the storytelling.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

The film is built on **one promise: "you ask, it's done"**. Three acts carry it: **the ask** (a question headline, then a request typing into a prompt bar), **the answer** (the result appears as a card, sharp and complete), and **the proof** (many results in rapid succession, then a payoff line and the name). The interface is the stage, but it is drawn, never captured: rounded cards, pills, a cursor, a caret, all in HTML/CSS/SVG so the camera can zoom anywhere and text stays crisp.

The rhythm is **long-short**: patient holds while something is understood (typing, reading the result) and violent compressions where something is proven (the punch-in on the button, 0.4 s proof cuts). The end card is the quietest shot in the film on purpose.

The "prompt" does not have to be an AI box: it is any place someone states what they want. For a shop it is an order note or a booking form; for a creator, a viewer's comment ("bikin versi pedas dong"); for a teacher, a student's question; in a small story, a character's wish. The "result" is the cake, the clean laundry, the booked slot, the drawing made from the comment, the worked answer, or the twist the wish brings.

Not a slideshow of product photos (the camera moves inside a UI world and every scene has cause and effect), not a dark tech stage talk (grounds are bright and warm as often as dark), not a real screen recording (nothing is a screenshot; no browser chrome, no OS), not kinetic typography alone (type punctuates, but the request → result action carries the film).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Flat grounds, no texture**: a near-white warm paper and its opposite, a near-black, plus the main colour as a ground for the payoff. A single soft radial glow of the main colour behind the subject is the only atmosphere. No grain, no gradients-as-decoration.
- **Cards**: big radii (48–60 px at 1080 wide), white on the light ground or a lifted dark surface on the dark ground, one soft long shadow (`0 40px 90px -40px`), optionally a 2 px hairline ring. Pills everywhere (badges, chips, buttons, status): radius 999 px.
- **The prompt bar** is the hero object: a large rounded card with a small grey label, the typed request in big type, a caret in the main colour, a round "+" on the left and a filled pill button in the main colour on the right.
- **The cursor** is a simple arrow (or a hand), dark with a light rim; it glides, never teleports, and squashes on click.
- **Defocus is a transition, not a look**: blur (8–16 px) is used only on entering elements (blur-in) and on the frame during a punch-in that ends in a cut. Readable text is never left blurred.
- **Light sweep** (a soft diagonal sheen crossing a card once) marks the result as finished.
- Illustrated subjects (a cake, a folded shirt, a cup, a sketch, a chart) are flat SVG shapes with two or three tones, sitting inside the card like a generated preview.

## 3. Colour logic

- `--latar`: the light ground; the ask and the end card live here. `--latar-2`: the cards and the prompt bar on it.
- `--teks`: ink on the light ground and its cards; `--teks-redup`: the bar's label, the "+" and the end card's small lines.
- `--gelap`: the opposite ground, where the answer lands so the cut reads as a flip of state. It is `var(--teks)`, so it stays the opposite of the brand's background: near-black under a light brand, near-white under a dark one. Text on it is `--teks-di-gelap` (`var(--latar)`); the lifted card on it is `--kartu-gelap` (a 5 % mix toward its text).
- `--utama`: the brand's strongest colour, reserved for the caret, the key words of the request, the action button, the price bar and the payoff ground. It is the thread the eye follows from ask to answer. Text on it is `--teks-di-utama`. As key-word colour on the light ground it goes through `--kata-kunci`, which falls back to `--teks` when the brand's main colour would not read there.
- `--aksen`: the highlight, used sparingly (one proof shot ground, candles, a badge). Text on it is `--teks-di-aksen`, which the script sets to whichever of `--teks` and `--latar` contrasts more, because a brand's accent can be light or dark.
- Fixed, whatever the brand: `--sukses`, a green only for a status pill ("Pesanan diterima"), its text mixed toward the ground's text so it reads on either; `--bayangan` (warm shadows on light) and `--bayangan-pekat` (the deep shadow under the dark card); the illustration colours (food, objects), which describe the subject, not the brand.
- The middle payoff word uses `--gelap` while it reads on `--utama` (at least 3:1, computed in the script), otherwise `--teks-di-utama`.

Light/dark alternation is structural: switch ground at every act boundary (light ask → dark answer → mixed proof → main-colour payoff → light end). In the proof burst, alternate grounds shot by shot (`--utama`, `--latar`, `--gelap`, `--aksen`, `--latar`) so every cut is visible even at a glance.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul` carries the headlines, card titles, proof labels, prices, payoff words, the end-card name and pill labels: one geometric sans in its heaviest weight (Poppins 800 by default), tight tracking (−3 to −5 % of size), line-height ~1.0. `--font-isi` carries the typed request, chips and body: the same family at 500.
- `--font-label` (Space Grotesk 500/700) is the look's interface face for small labels, order numbers, the status pill and the brand pill; it stays when a brand brings its own fonts, so the drawn UI keeps reading as UI. A handwritten face (`--font-tangan`, Caveat) only where it is diegetic: writing on a cake, a note.
- When the brand has no fonts, stay with geometric or grotesk sans faces (Poppins, Space Grotesk, Archivo Black for headlines); condensed display faces break the interface feel.
- **Sentence case**, short: the hook is a question of 3–5 words; proof labels are 1–2 words plus a price; the payoff is three one-word sentences.
- Sizes at 1080 × 1920: hook 120–140 px, typed request 56–64 px, card titles 70–80 px, proof labels 110–120 px, payoff words 220–260 px, end-card name 120–130 px. Nothing under ~38 px. A wider brand face needs these about 15 % smaller.
- **Reveals**: headline words blur-in and rise (y 40 → 0, blur 16 → 0, scale 0.96 → 1, 0.45 s power3.out, stagger 0.12 s); the request types character by character, its last phrase switching to the main colour; payoff words slam in from scale 1.6 with blur.

## 5. Motion quality

Numbers from the measured references (see the last section):

- **Shot length**: median shot ≈ 3 s for explanatory shots; proof bursts at 0.3–0.5 s per cut. Typical density ≈ 14–15 cuts per minute overall, so a 15 s vertical has 8–11 cuts with most of them packed into the proof burst.
- **Camera moves are short**: median move ≈ 0.45 s; a big punch-in takes ≈ 0.75 s.
- **Push-ins**: a gentle push while something is read reaches ≈ 1.19× (median measured zoom-in); a dive toward a button or icon reaches 1.6–1.7× (90th percentile ≈ 1.68×; the strongest measured ≈ 2.4–2.5×).
- **Pull-outs**: a reveal pull-back is ≈ 0.84× (median measured zoom-out), used right after a hard cut so the result "settles" into frame.
- **Eases (fitted to the measured camera)**: `sine.out` and `power1.out` for pushes and settles, `circ.out` for the landing after a cut, `power2.inOut` for dives between two points, `none` for micro punch-ins inside a burst, `sine.in` / `power1.in` only for an accelerating move that ends in a cut.
- **Element entrances** 0.3–0.6 s: cards `back.out(1.5–1.6)` from scale 0.9; chips and status pills stagger 0.08–0.12 s; counters run 0.8–1.2 s `power3.out`.
- **Exits are cuts**, not fades. A punch-in that accelerates (`power2.in`) and blurs for the last 0.25 s hands over to the next shot on the cut.
- Typing speed: ~12–15 characters per second, linear, with a blinking caret (0.25 s on/off).
- What never moves: the ground. The camera moves the whole layer; elements inside the UI only enter, react to a click, or count.

## 6. Camera grammar

A virtual camera over a flat UI layer (translate + scale with the focus point mapped to frame centre). Vocabulary, not a route.

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Slow push while typing (1.0 → 1.1–1.2×, sine/power1.out; stop before the bar's edges crop the typed text) | "this is where you speak" | an order being written; a viewer's comment; a student's question; a booking form |
| Dive-zoom to the button (→ 1.6–1.7×, power2.inOut, then accelerate + blur into a cut) | the decisive tap | "Pesan", "Kirim", "Booking", "Mulai belajar", "Tanya" |
| Hard cut + settle pull-out (1.2 → 1.0×, circ.out) | it's already done | the result card landing; a confirmation; the finished piece; the answer |
| Micro punch per proof cut (1.1 → 1.0×, 0.35 s) | "and this, and this" | a range of products, menus or outfits; a creator's past results; solved questions |
| Lateral carousel slide between cards | variety in one system | sizes, flavours, packages; versions of one idea |
| Pull-back from the payoff (→ ~0.85×) | the whole promise in one view | a three-word slogan; a before/after summary; the moral of the story |
| Near-static end card with a 1.04 → 1.0 drift | calm after the rush | name, call to action, address or handle |

Framing: one subject at a time, centred, with generous margins (≥ 70 px at 1080). The thing being typed or tapped is always the focus point of the camera. Transitions: hard cuts and zoom-throughs only; no dissolves, no page-turn wipes.

## 7. Native moves

A menu: use the ones the message needs.

- **The typed request.** A question headline blurs in word by word, then the exact request types into the prompt bar, the specific part in the main colour. *Fits content like:* a cake shop taking custom-writing orders; a viewer's comment typed as the request for a creator's next video; a student's question typed into a tutor's study bar; a character's wish that starts a short story.
- **Dive to the button.** The cursor glides to the action pill, the camera dives at it, the click squashes, the frame accelerates into blur and cuts. *Fits content like:* "Pesan" at an online food stall; "Booking" for a barbershop; "Kirim" on a chat order; "Mulai" on a class; "Tanya" in a Q&A series.
- **The answer card.** Hard cut to the opposite ground; the result card lands with a settle pull-out, a green status pill, details as chips, a price or figure that counts up, one light sweep. *Fits content like:* an order confirmation with pickup time; a laundry status "Siap diambil"; the drawing a creator made from a comment; the worked answer to a homework question with its steps as chips.
- **Proof burst.** Four to six 0.4 s shots, each a single item with a two-word label and a price or detail, grounds alternating light / dark / main / highlight. *Fits content like:* the week's cake range; five outfits of a new drop; five comments turned into five finished pieces; five questions a tutor solved this week; five moments of a day in a short story.
- **Three-word payoff.** On the main colour, three one-word sentences slam in 0.4 s apart, then the camera pulls back and the first two dim. *Fits content like:* "Ketik. Pesan. Jadi."; "Antar. Cuci. Beres."; "Komen. Request. Jadi." for a creator; "Tanya. Paham. Bisa." for a class.
- **The quiet end.** Light ground, a mark pops, the name and one line rise with blur, an inverse pill with the address, link or handle, almost no motion for the last two seconds. *Fits content like:* any closing, especially after a dense proof burst: a shop's site; "Follow untuk part 2"; a class sign-up link.
- **Counted proof.** Instead of items, numbers: orders today, minutes to ready, ratings, each as a 0.4 s cut. *Fits content like:* a laundry's "selesai 6 jam"; a catering's "1.200 porsi bulan ini"; a channel's "300 request selesai"; a course's "4,9 dari 2.000 murid".

## 8. Pitfalls

- The push while typing crops the request: keep it at 1.1–1.12×, focused on the bar, and stop before its edges reach the last line.
- A request over ~60 characters wraps past three lines at 60 px and the typing drags past 4 s. Type only the specific part; the rest goes in the headline.
- Leaving readable text blurred, or holding a full-frame blur: blur only entrances and the last 0.25 s before a cut, 10–16 px at most. A long `filter: blur()` on the whole frame also drops frames in the preview.
- Dissolves and fades between shots kill "it's already done": every scene change is a hard cut or a zoom-through.
- Proof cuts longer than ~0.6 s turn the burst into a slideshow; more than a two-word label and a price cannot be read in 0.4 s; two proof shots in a row on the same ground hide the cut.
- Anything that looks captured: browser chrome, status bars, real app logos or interfaces. Draw the interface.
- A busy ending: the end card is the quietest shot. One or two pill breaths, then nothing new in the last 1.5 s.
- Text on the opposite ground or the highlight set in `--teks`: under another brand it disappears. Use `--teks-di-gelap` and `--teks-di-aksen`.
- A cursor that teleports or clicks without the squash: the decisive tap is the hinge of the story.

## Measured from the references

- Films: 8 (cluster of 109)
- Median length: 42 s (cluster median 45 s)
- Cuts per minute: median 14.4 (range 4.5–46.2)
- Median shot: 3.1 s (range 0.8–10 s); proof bursts 0.2–0.4 s per cut
- Tempo of the cut rhythm: median ≈ 128 bpm
- Camera moves measured: 170; median duration 0.46 s; big punch-ins (> 1.3×) median 0.75 s
- Zoom: median push-in 1.19×, 90th percentile 1.68×, max ≈ 2.55×; median pull-out 0.84×
- Most common fitted eases: `sine.out`, `circ.out`, `power1.out`, `none`, then `power2.inOut`, `sine.in`, `power1.in`, `power2.out`
- Light/dark ground switches: present in half of the films

# Instant order: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 2, medium 3.1, long 4.5.

## hook

- en: a question blurs in word by word, the request types into a rounded bar, the camera dives at the button and blurs into a cut
- id: pertanyaan muncul per kata dari blur, permintaan diketik di kotak bulat, kamera menyelam ke tombol lalu potong

## problem

- en: the old way as a cluttered chat or form card, a slow push-in while it is read, then a hard cut to the opposite ground
- id: cara lama sebagai kartu chat atau formulir yang ruwet, kamera mendorong pelan, lalu potong ke latar sebaliknya

## fact

- en: one short sentence-case line rises out of blur on a flat ground, a gentle push to 1.1× while it is read
- id: satu kalimat pendek muncul dari blur di latar polos, kamera mendorong pelan sampai 1,1× selama dibaca

## step

- en: the cursor glides to a pill or field, squashes on the click, and a status pill pops in on the card
- id: kursor meluncur ke tombol atau kolom, mengempis saat diklik, lalu pill status meletup di kartu

## compare

- en: two cards on light and dark grounds; a lateral slide carries the eye across and settles on the better one
- id: dua kartu di latar terang dan gelap; geser ke samping lalu berhenti di yang lebih baik

## number

- en: a figure on a card counts up 1 s; several figures are separate 0.4 s cuts on alternating grounds
- id: angka di kartu dihitung naik 1 detik; beberapa angka jadi potongan 0,4 detik dengan latar bergantian

## proof

- en: a burst of 0.4 s cuts, one item each with a two-word label and a price, grounds alternating every cut
- id: rentetan potongan 0,4 detik, satu item per potongan dengan label dua kata dan harga, latar berganti tiap potongan

## offer

- en: hard cut to the opposite ground: the result card settles in, chips stagger, the price counts up, one light sweep
- id: potong keras ke latar sebaliknya: kartu hasil mendarat, chip berurutan, harga dihitung naik, satu kilau lewat

## cta

- en: quiet light end card: mark pops, name rises out of blur, an inverse pill with the contact, held 2 s
- id: penutup terang yang tenang: logo meletup, nama muncul dari blur, pill kontras berisi kontak, diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: three one-word sentences slam in on the main colour, the camera pulls back and the first two dim; held 2 s
- id: tiga kalimat satu kata menghentak di warna utama, kamera mundur, dua kata awal meredup; diam 2 detik

        typed.innerHTML = esc(a) + (b ? '<span class="hot">' + esc(b) + "</span>" : "");

      const shots = ["#c1", "#c2", "#c3", "#c4", "#c5"];

        const k = Math.round(ty.n);
        if (k === shown) return; // tulis ulang hanya saat huruf bertambah, bukan tiap frame
